name: Chart
purpose: Visualizes a metric with a token-branded, accessible chart so people can understand trends, comparisons, composition, or events.
neverUseFor: Raw ECharts options or a product-specific chart renderer
Precise audit values without an accompanying Table
rationale: Chart wraps the charting engine behind a token-branded API (ADR-021) so series colors, axes and typography come from --helix-* tokens rather than raw library options, and every chart ships with a labelled data table for 1.1.1 Non-text Content. Consumers describe the metric; Helix owns the rendering, palette and accessibility. The palette is all blue: series 1 is the primary Button's blue and every next series is a blue far from the one before it, never a near tone, and every series meets 3:1 on the page with no outline — dark blues alternate in light mode, light blues in dark mode (ADR-021 amendment). Stacked segments and donut slices are split by a page-colored gap. Charts draw in on load — lines sweep over semantic.duration.draw with each point appearing as the line reaches it, bars and series follow semantic.duration.stagger apart, eased with semantic.easing.gentle — and render finished under prefers-reduced-motion. The area fill fades from component.chart.area-opacity to transparent. A donut whose categories stay the same but whose values change does not draw in again: each slice eases to its new angle over component.chart.duration-update with component.chart.easing-update, the gaps between slices staying even (transitions.dev donut chart).

mayExtendLocally: Choose the chart type and data series from the documented props
Pair a Chart with a Table for precise audit values
Compose Charts inside Cards to build dashboards
mustEscalateToDS: Passing raw engine options or a product-specific renderer
Adding new chart types or series colors outside the token palette

anatomy.description: Apache ECharts canvas with accessible name.
Legend below the canvas. With two or more entries it is a group of toggle buttons.
One series (or donut category): a ghost-style toggle button with aria-pressed when there are several, a static label when there is one.
Square series-color swatch — unchanged while the series is hidden; only the item's text turns gray.
Visually hidden source-data table for non-visual access — hidden on a wrapper div (a table ignores height/overflow). Missing values read "No data", never 0.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional className for the root element.

label.reason: the chart's accessible name — aria-label of the canvas and the caption of the hidden data table, never drawn; the visible legend texts are each series' name (series → ChartLegendItem label)

categories.note: donut only: each slice's name, in the legend (the other types draw categories as the axis labels)

series.note: each series' name, in the legend (not on the donut)

placement..reason: where the hover box sits from the pointer line (top / right / bottom / left) — ECharts places it next to the cursor, Figma needs a fixed choice

figma.hover: Exception (owner's decision 2026-10-21): code shows ECharts' hover only while the pointer is over the chart, but it's part of how the chart looks, so Figma draws it — state=hover × placement. on every variant (24 variants + 6 at rest). chart-pointer (absolute over the plot, left padding bound to a spacing variable — change it to move the line along the axis) holds chart-pointer-line (dashed 1px, border/neutral; none on the donut) and chart-tooltip (fill/page, 1px border/neutral, radius/l, spacing/s padding, shadow / s; title + one row per series: marker chart/series/n, name, value Body / m / Semibold). Code sets the same tokens on ECharts' tooltip and axisPointer (Chart.tsx).

properties.name: variant
properties.description: One Chart variant per type, each drawn with the matching story's sample data (Line, Area, Bar, Stacked Bar, Donut, Timeline). The canvas is a static drawing of what ECharts renders: series in chart/series/1…6, axis and split lines border/neutral, axis labels Body / s / Regular text/neutral/light; stacked segments and donut slices separated by a fill/page gap. The area fill is the series color at the area-opacity (15%) as layer opacity — Figma can't bind a variable to a gradient stop, so the fade to transparent isn't drawn.

properties.name: state
properties.description: On ChartLegendItem (the legend toggle): hover/press are CSS pseudo-classes in code (fill/secondary/interactive/default and /hover, text/neutral); focus is the global focus ring.

properties.name: pressed
properties.description: On ChartLegendItem: a hidden series (aria-pressed false) keeps its swatch and turns its name text/disabled. A VARIANT, not a BOOLEAN — it changes a color, not a part's visibility.

properties.name: label
properties.description: On ChartLegendItem: the series (or donut category) name.

figma.structure: Chart = chart-root (vertical, 560 wide like the stories, 8px to the legend = spacing/xs) > chart-canvas (280 high = the height prop's default) + chart-legend (wrapping row, centered, 4px apart = spacing/2xs) of ChartLegendItem instances. ChartLegendItem = 4/8 padding (spacing/2xs, spacing/xs), 8px gap, radius/m, a 1px border that is always transparent (hidden stroke, border-always), a 12px swatch (spacing/s, radius/xs) in the series' chart/series/N — overridden per instance — and the name in Body / s / Regular. The data table (chart-data) is visually hidden in code and not drawn.

LegendToggle.reason: click on a legend item hides its series — behaviour test

a11y.role: img with labelled data table; legend entries are toggle buttons (aria-pressed) when there are several
keyboardNav: Tab — moves focus through the legend's toggle buttons
Space/Enter — shows or hides the focused series
